<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Extend\Internal;

use CoreX\Access\Contracts\RoleMatrixCompiler;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\EntityRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\ModuleRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Events\ModuleDisabled;
use CoreX\Modules\Events\ModuleEnabled;

/**
 * Ties `aut_role_matrix` compilation to module lifecycle (AC-27, D112/D113):
 * on ANY enable/disable, {@see RoleMatrixCompiler::recompileAll()} re-runs,
 * so active-entity checks are re-evaluated against
 * the module's new state. This class creates NO `aut_role_matrix` rows
 * itself (D113 — the merger only merges the SURFACE, modules write the
 * matrix); the rows a disabled module's entities leave behind stay in the
 * table for re-enable.
 *
 * `merge()` also validates `CompiledRegistry::$permissions` declarations
 * against {@see EntityRegistry}: a declaration whose `entity` is unknown to
 * the registry cannot be attributed to any module (the compiled slot
 * carries no module attribution of its own, findings/P2.9-seam-inventory
 * §6) and is skipped fail-closed — surfaced as a warning in the return
 * value, never a log (same contract as {@see CoreX\Access\Matrix\Internal\MatrixValidator}).
 *
 * @internal spec: B-11 §4 п.2/п.4, P2.21 D112/D113, AC-27
 */
final readonly class PermissionsMerger
{
    public function __construct(
        private ModuleRegistry $modules,
        private EntityRegistry $entities,
        private RoleMatrixCompiler $compiler,
    ) {}

    public function __invoke(ModuleEnabled|ModuleDisabled $event): void
    {
        $this->merge();
    }

    /** @return list<string> warnings for Extend\Permissions declarations whose entity is unknown to EntityRegistry */
    public function merge(): array
    {
        $warnings = [];

        foreach ($this->modules->compiled()->permissions as $declaration) {
            if (! $this->entities->has($declaration->entity)) {
                $warnings[] = sprintf(
                    "Extend\\Permissions declares unknown entity '%s' — declaration ignored, no matrix row can attribute to a module.",
                    $declaration->entity,
                );
            }
        }

        $this->compiler->recompileAll();

        return $warnings;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use CoreX\Access\Access\Laravel\PrincipalIdentity;
use CoreX\Access\Contracts\AccessChecker;
use CoreX\Access\Enums\PrincipalType;
use CoreX\Access\Enums\Scope;
use CoreX\Access\Laravel\ScopeResolver;
use CoreX\Access\Roles\Internal\Models\Role;
use CoreX\Access\Roles\Internal\Models\RoleAssignment;
use CoreX\Access\Roles\Internal\Models\RoleMatrixRow;
use CoreX\Access\Tests\Stubs\Deal;
use CoreX\Access\Tests\Stubs\FakeModuleRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\ModuleRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Data\EntityDefinition;
use CoreX\Modules\Enums\Capability;
use CoreX\Modules\Testing\ArrayEntityRegistry;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

uses()->group('pg');

beforeEach(function (): void {
    $this->resetPgSchema();
    $this->migrateAutSchema();
    $this->migrateFixtures();

    app(ArrayEntityRegistry::class)->register(new EntityDefinition(
        handle: 'crm.deal', model: Deal::class, table: 'deals', module: 'corex/access-tests',
        labelSingular: 'Deal', labelPlural: 'Deals',
        capabilities: [Capability::Ownable, Capability::WorkspaceScoped], fields: [], titleAttribute: null,
    ));
    app()->instance(ModuleRegistry::class, new FakeModuleRegistry(['corex/access-tests']));
});

function nativeGrant(PrincipalIdentity $principal, ?string $expiresAt = null, ?string $revokedAt = null, string $entityKey = 'crm.deal'): void
{
    DB::table('aut_direct_grants')->insert([
        'id' => (string) Str::uuid7(),
        'principal_type' => $principal->principalType()->value,
        'principal_id' => $principal->principalId(),
        'permission_key' => "app.{$entityKey}.read",
        'expires_at' => $expiresAt,
        'revoked_at' => $revokedAt,
    ]);
}

it('honours an active native direct grant on capability, record and builder paths without a role', function (): void {
    $principal = new PrincipalIdentity(PrincipalType::User, (string) Str::uuid7());
    $record = Deal::query()->create(['id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'owner_id' => (string) Str::uuid7()]);
    nativeGrant($principal);
    $checker = app(AccessChecker::class);

    expect($checker->allowed($principal, 'crm.deal', 'read'))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($checker->scopeFor($principal, 'crm.deal', 'read'))->toBe(Scope::None)
        ->and($checker->canOnRecord($principal, 'read', $record))->toBeTrue()
        ->and(app(ScopeResolver::class)->apply(Deal::query(), $principal, 'crm.deal', 'read')->pluck('id')->all())->toBe([$record->id]);
});

it('denies expired and revoked native direct grants', function (string $expiresAt, string $revokedAt): void {
    $principal = new PrincipalIdentity(PrincipalType::User, (string) Str::uuid7());
    $record = Deal::query()->create(['id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'owner_id' => $principal->principalId()]);
    nativeGrant($principal, $expiresAt ?: null, $revokedAt ?: null);
    $checker = app(AccessChecker::class);

    expect($checker->allowed($principal, 'crm.deal', 'read'))->toBeFalse()
        ->and($checker->canOnRecord($principal, 'read', $record))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(app(ScopeResolver::class)->apply(Deal::query(), $principal, 'crm.deal', 'read')->pluck('id')->all())->toBeEmpty();
})->with([
    'expired' => [now()->subMinute()->toDateTimeString(), ''],
    'revoked' => ['', now()->subMinute()->toDateTimeString()],
]);

it('denies all four access paths for an inactive entity even with a matrix row and direct grant', function (bool $registered): void {
    $modules = new FakeModuleRegistry($registered ? [] : ['corex/access-tests']);
    app()->instance(ModuleRegistry::class, $modules);
    $entityKey = $registered ? 'crm.deal' : 'ghost.deal';
    $principal = new PrincipalIdentity(PrincipalType::User, (string) Str::uuid7());
    $role = Role::query()->create([
        'slug' => 'role-'.Str::uuid7(), 'name' => 'Role', 'is_system' => false,
        'assignable_to' => [PrincipalType::User->value],
    ]);
    RoleMatrixRow::query()->create(['role_id' => $role->id, 'entity_key' => $entityKey, 'action' => 'read', 'scope' => 'account']);
    RoleAssignment::query()->create(['role_id' => $role->id, 'principal_type' => 'user', 'principal_id' => $principal->principalId()]);
    $record = Deal::query()->create(['id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'owner_id' => $principal->principalId()]);
    nativeGrant($principal, entityKey: $entityKey);
    $checker = app(AccessChecker::class);

    $recordForCheck = $registered ? $record : new class extends Model {};

    expect(DB::table('aut_direct_grants')->where('permission_key', "app.{$entityKey}.read")->exists())->toBeTrue()
        ->and($checker->allowed($principal, $entityKey, 'read'))->toBeFalse()
        ->and($checker->scopeFor($principal, $entityKey, 'read'))->toBe(Scope::None)
        ->and($checker->canOnRecord($principal, 'read', $recordForCheck))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(app(ScopeResolver::class)->apply(Deal::query(), $principal, $entityKey, 'read')->pluck('id')->all())->toBeEmpty();
})->with([
    'registered entity with disabled module' => [true],
    'unknown entity key' => [false],
]);

в AzGuard напрямую.

Удалённые роли всё

корректно, если дефолт совпадает с `az_guard_role_permissions`.

Слушатель удаляет записи через модель `RolePermission`, которая использует имя таблицы по умолчанию из модели, а не из конфига. При изменении имени таблицы через пин возникает риск рассогласования.

Blade-директивы вызывают `hasScopedRole` и `hasScopedPermission` на `auth()->user()`. Эти методы, вероятно, пришли из трейта `HasPermissions` AzGuard. Спецификация требует, чтобы `PrincipalIdentity` не реализовывал контракты AzGuard.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal;

use AzGuard\Configuration\Config;
use AzGuard\Models\Role as AzGuardRole;
use AzGuard\Models\RolePermission;
use Override;

/**
 * @corex-model-extension AzGuard role configuration adapter; preserves Role columns/relations and overrides only the configured roles table.
 * AzGuard's own `Role` model does not read `table_names.roles` itself (only
 * {@see RolePermission} does) — the config pin D104 sets
 * (`az_guard_roles`) would otherwise be inert. Bound as `az-guard.models.role`
 * (AccessAzguardServiceProvider), AzGuard's own `Config::roleModel()` seam
 * (`config/az-guard.php` "Models" — "Replace with your own subclasses"),
 * never a fork of the package (D15).
 */
final class AzGuardRoleModel extends AzGuardRole
{
    #[Override]
    public function getTable(): string
    {
        return Config::rolesTable();
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal;

use AzGuard\Models\Role;
use CoreX\Config\Laravel\ConfigurationValidator;

/** @internal Immutable configuration for bridge composition. */
final readonly class AccessAzguardOptions
{
    /** @param class-string<Role>|null $roleModel */
    public function __construct(
        public bool $bindPermissionLayer,
        public string $rolesTable,
        public string $morphType,
        public ?string $roleModel,
    ) {}

    /** @param array<array-key, mixed> $config */
    public static function fromArray(array $config): self
    {
        $violations = new ConfigurationValidator;
        $bindPermissionLayer = $config['bind_permission_layer'] ?? true;

        if (! is_bool($bindPermissionLayer)) {
            $violations->add('bind_permission_layer', 'must be a boolean');
            $bindPermissionLayer = false;
        }

        $pins = self::section($violations, 'azguard_pins', $config['azguard_pins'] ?? []);
        $tables = self::section($violations, 'azguard_pins.table_names', $pins['table_names'] ?? []);
        $columns = self::section($violations, 'azguard_pins.column_names', $pins['column_names'] ?? []);
        $models = self::section($violations, 'azguard_pins.models', $pins['models'] ?? []);
        $rolesTable = $tables['roles'] ?? 'az_guard_roles';

        if (! is_string($rolesTable) || trim($rolesTable) === '') {
            $violations->add('azguard_pins.table_names.roles', 'must be a non-empty string');
            $rolesTable = 'az_guard_roles';
        }

        $morphType = $columns['morph_type'] ?? 'uuid';

        if (! in_array($morphType, ['int', 'ulid', 'uuid'], true)) {
            $violations->add('azguard_pins.column_names.morph_type', 'must be int, ulid or uuid');
            $morphType = 'uuid';
        }

        $roleModel = array_key_exists('role', $models) ? $models['role'] : AzGuardRoleModel::class;

        if ($roleModel !== null && (! is_string($roleModel) || ! is_a($roleModel, Role::class, true))) {
            $violations->add('azguard_pins.models.role', 'must be an AzGuard role class or null');
            $roleModel = AzGuardRoleModel::class;
        }

        $violations->failIfAny();

        return new self(
            bindPermissionLayer: $bindPermissionLayer,
            rolesTable: $rolesTable,
            morphType: $morphType,
            roleModel: $roleModel,
        );
    }

    /** @return array<array-key, mixed> */
    private static function section(ConfigurationValidator $violations, string $path, mixed $value): array
    {
        if (is_array($value)) {
            return $value;
        }

        $violations->add($path, 'must be an array');

        return [];
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal;

use AzGuard\Contracts\ContextGuard;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\EntityRegistry;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Override;

/**
 * Implements AzGuard's ContextGuard seam (the binding AzGuard expects from an
 * external package) so `$user->hasPermissionIn($type, $id, $permission)` works:
 * the context entity is resolved through axiomasoft/corex's EntityRegistry (single
 * morph source, ADR-003), and the check passes when the user has the
 * permission scoped to that entity, or globally within the panel.
 *
 * Tenant isolation of the resolved entity is physical (DB-per-account, B-11):
 * an entity loaded here already came from its account's database.
 */
final class TenantContextGuard implements ContextGuard
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly EntityRegistry $entities,
    ) {}

    #[Override]
    public function checkInContext(
        Authenticatable $user,
        string $contextType,
        int|string $contextId,
        string $permission,
        string $panelId,
    ): bool {
        $entity = $this->resolveContext($contextType, $contextId);

        if (! $entity instanceof Model) {
            return false;
        }

        $scopedCheck = [$user, 'hasScopedPermission'];

        if (is_callable($scopedCheck) && $scopedCheck($permission, $entity) === true) {
            return true;
        }

        $globalCheck = [$user, 'hasPermission'];

        return is_callable($globalCheck) && $globalCheck($permission, $panelId) === true;
    }

    private function resolveContext(string $contextType, int|string $contextId): ?Model
    {
        if (! $this->entities->has($contextType)) {
            return null;
        }

        $class = $this->entities->get($contextType)->model;
        $instance = new $class;

        if (! $instance instanceof Model) {
            return null;
        }

        return $instance->newQuery()->whereKey($contextId)->first();
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal;

use AzGuard\Contracts\PermissionLayer;
use AzGuard\Registry\Values\PermissionSet;
use CoreX\Context\Contracts\TenancyManager;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable;
use Override;

/**
 * Cache-discriminator layer (D101) — apply() is the identity function
 * (AutMatrixGrantSource already scoped its keys to the active workspace at
 * the source, so this layer never narrows); its role is purely to tag the
 * resolver's per-request cache entry so workspace 42 and workspace 99 never
 * share one (findings/P2.8-azguard-inventory-2026-07-26.md §6) — without
 * it, a resolved set for one workspace would leak into the next request-
 * local lookup for another.
 */
final readonly class WorkspacePermissionLayer implements PermissionLayer
{
    public function __construct(
        private TenancyManager $tenancyManager,
    ) {}

    #[Override]
    public function apply(PermissionSet $global, Authenticatable $user, string $panelId): PermissionSet
    {
        return $global;
    }

    #[Override]
    public function cacheDiscriminator(string $panelId): string
    {
        return $this->tenancyManager->context()?->workspace->id ?? '';
    }
}

namespace CoreX\Context\Data;

use CoreX\Attributes\Api;

/**
 * The current account/workspace pair a request or job runs under. Resolved
 * by axiomasoft/corex-tenancy; boxed installs get a constant singleton via
 * {@see SingleAccountResolver}.
 *
 * Contract: B-10 §3.1, B-11 §3.1 (owner: B-11).
 */
#[Api(since: '1.0')]
final readonly class TenantContext
{
    public function __construct(
        public AccountRef $account,
        public ?WorkspaceRef $workspace = null,
        private bool $boxed = false,
    ) {}

    /**
     * True iff this context was produced by {@see SingleAccountResolver}
     * (boxed installs), not by a real P2 tenancy resolver.
     */
    public function isBoxed(): bool
    {
        return $this->boxed;
    }

    public function forWorkspace(WorkspaceRef $workspace): self
    {
        return new self($this->account, $workspace, $this->boxed);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Access\Internal;

use CoreX\Access\Enums\Scope;
use CoreX\Access\Exceptions\ScopeCapabilityMismatch;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\EntityRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Enums\Capability;
use Illuminate\Database\Connection;
use Illuminate\Database\ConnectionResolverInterface;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Builder as SchemaBuilder;

/**
 * Normalizes a compiled Scope against the entity's declared capabilities
 * (B-11 §4 п.3, D114) before it reaches {@see ScopePredicate}: own/dept/
 * dept_tree require Capability::Ownable, workspace requires
 * Capability::WorkspaceScoped. Letter-only compliance ("no capability =>
 * account") silently widens access when the physical column DOES exist and
 * the entity's declaration is simply missing — that case fails closed with
 * {@see ScopeCapabilityMismatch} instead (declaration drift is a bug in the
 * entity's own registration, not a runtime access decision). Only degrades
 * to `account` when the column is genuinely absent — there is nothing to
 * narrow by.
 *
 * Memoized per (entity_key, scope) for the life of the request so
 * `Schema::hasColumn()` does not hit the schema on every call.
 *
 * @internal spec: B-11 §4 п.3, P2.9 D114
 */
final class ScopeAvailability
{
    /** @var array<string, Scope> */
    private array $memo = [];

    public function __construct(
        private readonly EntityRegistry $entities,
        private readonly ConnectionResolverInterface $connections,
    ) {}

    public function normalize(string $entityKey, Scope $scope): Scope
    {
        $requirement = $this->requirementFor($scope);

        if ($requirement === null) {
            return $scope;
        }

        $memoKey = "{$entityKey}|{$scope->value}";

        if (array_key_exists($memoKey, $this->memo)) {
            return $this->memo[$memoKey];
        }

        return $this->memo[$memoKey] = $this->resolve($entityKey, $scope, $requirement);
    }

    /** @return array{capability: Capability, column: string}|null */
    private function requirementFor(Scope $scope): ?array
    {
        return match ($scope) {
            Scope::Own, Scope::Dept, Scope::DeptTree => ['capability' => Capability::Ownable, 'column' => 'owner_id'],
            Scope::Workspace => ['capability' => Capability::WorkspaceScoped, 'column' => 'workspace_id'],
            default => null,
        };
    }

    /** @param array{capability: Capability, column: string} $requirement */
    private function resolve(string $entityKey, Scope $scope, array $requirement): Scope
    {
        // Unknown entity_key: not "widen to account" — the entity is not
        // registered at all, so there is no capability to check. Mirrors
        // canOnRecord()'s own fail-closed unresolved-entity handling.
        if (! $this->entities->has($entityKey)) {
            return Scope::None;
        }

        $entity = $this->entities->get($entityKey);

        if (in_array($requirement['capability'], $entity->capabilities, true)) {
            return $scope;
        }

        if (! $this->schema()->hasColumn($entity->table, $requirement['column'])) {
            return Scope::Account;
        }

        throw ScopeCapabilityMismatch::forScope($entityKey, $scope->value, $requirement['capability']->value, $requirement['column']);
    }

    private function schema(): SchemaBuilder
    {
        /** @var Connection */
        $connection = $this->connections->connection();

        return $connection->getSchemaBuilder();
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

use CoreX\Access\Enums\PrincipalType;
use CoreX\Access\Matrix\Events\RoleMatrixCompiled;
use CoreX\Access\Matrix\Internal\DatabaseRoleMatrixCompiler;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Event;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

uses()->group('pg');

beforeEach(function (): void {
    $this->resetPgSchema();
    $this->migrateAutSchema();

    app(ArrayEntityRegistry::class)->register(new EntityDefinition(
        handle: 'crm.deal', model: Deal::class, table: 'deals', module: 'corex/access-tests',
        labelSingular: 'Deal', labelPlural: 'Deals', capabilities: [Capability::Ownable], fields: [], titleAttribute: null,
    ));
    app()->instance(ModuleRegistry::class, new FakeModuleRegistry(['corex/access-tests']));
});

function nativeRole(): Role
{
    return Role::query()->create([
        'slug' => 'role-'.Str::uuid7(),
        'name' => 'Role',
        'is_system' => false,
        'assignable_to' => [PrincipalType::User->value],
    ]);
}

it('dispatches the native compilation event synchronously inside the tenant transaction', function (): void {
    $role = nativeRole();
    RoleMatrixRow::query()->create(['role_id' => $role->id, 'entity_key' => 'crm.deal', 'action' => 'read', 'scope' => 'account']);
    $seen = [];

    Event::listen(RoleMatrixCompiled::class, function (RoleMatrixCompiled $event) use (&$seen): void {
        $seen[] = [
            $event->roleId,
            DB::transactionLevel(),
            DB::table('aut_role_matrix')->where('role_id', $event->roleId)->count(),
        ];
    });

    app(DatabaseRoleMatrixCompiler::class)->compile($role->id);

    expect($seen)->toBe([[$role->id, 1, 1]])
        ->and(RoleMatrixRow::query()->where('role_id', $role->id)->count())->toBe(1);
});

it('rolls back a listener write and leaves the scope version unchanged when a listener fails', function (): void {
    $role = nativeRole();
    $versions = app(ScopeMapVersion::class);
    $initial = $versions->current($role->id);

    Event::listen(RoleMatrixCompiled::class, function (RoleMatrixCompiled $event): void {
        DB::table('aut_roles')->where('id', $event->roleId)->update(['name' => 'Uncommitted']);

        throw new RuntimeException('listener failure');
    });

    expect(fn () => app(DatabaseRoleMatrixCompiler::class)->compile($role->id))
        ->toThrow(RuntimeException::class, 'listener failure');
    expect($role->fresh()->name)->toBe('Role')
        ->and($versions->current($role->id))->toBe($initial);
});

it('invalidates scope only after outer commit and never after rollback', function (): void {
    $role = nativeRole();
    $versions = app(ScopeMapVersion::class);
    $initial = $versions->current($role->id);

    DB::beginTransaction();
    app(DatabaseRoleMatrixCompiler::class)->compile($role->id);
    expect($versions->current($role->id))->toBe($initial);
    DB::rollBack();
    expect($versions->current($role->id))->toBe($initial);

    DB::beginTransaction();
    app(DatabaseRoleMatrixCompiler::class)->compile($role->id);
    expect($versions->current($role->id))->toBe($initial);
    DB::commit();
    expect($versions->current($role->id))->toBe($initial + 1);
});

it('recompileAll emits once for every role and retains native matrix rows', function (): void {
    $first = nativeRole();
    $second = nativeRole();
    RoleMatrixRow::query()->create(['role_id' => $first->id, 'entity_key' => 'crm.deal', 'action' => 'read', 'scope' => 'account']);
    $events = [];

    Event::listen(RoleMatrixCompiled::class, function (RoleMatrixCompiled $event) use (&$events): void {
        $events[] = $event->roleId;
    });
    app(DatabaseRoleMatrixCompiler::class)->recompileAll();

    expect($events)->toEqualCanonicalizing([$first->id, $second->id])
        ->and(RoleMatrixRow::query()->where('role_id', $first->id)->count())->toBe(1);
});

it('warns when a role assignable to agent uses own scope', function (): void {
    $role = nativeRole();
    $role->assignable_to = [PrincipalType::User->value, PrincipalType::Agent->value];
    $role->save();
    RoleMatrixRow::query()->create(['role_id' => $role->id, 'entity_key' => 'crm.deal', 'action' => 'read', 'scope' => 'own']);

    $warnings = app(MatrixValidator::class)->validate(RoleMatrixData::role($role->id));

    expect($warnings)->not->toBeEmpty()
        ->and($warnings[0])->toContain('agent');
});

it('returns no agent-scope warning for a user-only role', function (): void {
    $role = nativeRole();
    RoleMatrixRow::query()->create(['role_id' => $role->id, 'entity_key' => 'crm.deal', 'action' => 'read', 'scope' => 'own']);

    expect(app(MatrixValidator::class)->validate(RoleMatrixData::role($role->id)))->toBeEmpty();
});

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Matrix\Internal;

use CoreX\Access\Enums\PrincipalType;
use CoreX\Access\Enums\Scope;
use CoreX\Access\Roles\Data\RoleMatrixEntry;
use CoreX\Access\Roles\Data\RoleView;
use CoreX\Access\Roles\Laravel\RoleMatrixData;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\EntityRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Enums\Capability;
use Illuminate\Database\Connection;
use Illuminate\Database\ConnectionResolverInterface;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Builder as SchemaBuilder;

/**
 * Warns (never throws) about two classes of matrix-row risk — the return
 * value is the whole contract, never a log:
 *
 * 1. A role assignable to agent/api_key carries own/dept/dept_tree rows:
 *    those scopes degrade to `none` for non-user principals (B-11 §5.5) — a
 *    role designed for agents should use workspace/account instead.
 * 2. (P2.9, D114) A row names own/dept/dept_tree/workspace on an entity
 *    whose table HAS the matching column (`owner_id`/`workspace_id`) but
 *    whose `EntityDefinition` never declared the matching capability
 *    (`Ownable`/`WorkspaceScoped`) — declaration drift that
 *    {@see CoreX\Access\Access\Internal\ScopeAvailability} would fail closed on at
 *    request time; this surfaces the same condition earlier, at
 *    matrix-authoring time.
 */
final readonly class MatrixValidator
{
    private const array OWNER_DEGRADED_SCOPES = [
        Scope::Own->value,
        Scope::Dept->value,
        Scope::DeptTree->value,
    ];

    /** @var array<string, array{capability: Capability, column: string}> */
    private const array SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT = [
        'own' => ['capability' => Capability::Ownable, 'column' => 'owner_id'],
        'dept' => ['capability' => Capability::Ownable, 'column' => 'owner_id'],
        'dept_tree' => ['capability' => Capability::Ownable, 'column' => 'owner_id'],
        'workspace' => ['capability' => Capability::WorkspaceScoped, 'column' => 'workspace_id'],
    ];

    public function __construct(
        private EntityRegistry $entities,
        private ConnectionResolverInterface $connections,
    ) {}

    /** @return list<string> */
    public function validate(RoleView $role): array
    {
        return [
            ...$this->degradedScopeWarnings($role),
            ...$this->capabilityDriftWarnings($role),
        ];
    }

    /** @return list<string> */
    private function degradedScopeWarnings(RoleView $role): array
    {
        $nonUserAssignable = array_values(array_diff($role->assignableTo, [PrincipalType::User->value]));

        if ($nonUserAssignable === []) {
            return [];
        }

        $hasDegradedScope = array_any(RoleMatrixData::matrix($role->id), static fn (RoleMatrixEntry $row): bool => in_array($row->scope->value, self::OWNER_DEGRADED_SCOPES, true));

        if (! $hasDegradedScope) {
            return [];
        }

        return [sprintf(
            "Role '%s' is assignable to %s, but its matrix uses own/dept/dept_tree scope — these degrade to none for non-user principals.",
            $role->slug,
            implode(', ', $nonUserAssignable),
        )];
    }

    /** @return list<string> */
    private function capabilityDriftWarnings(RoleView $role): array
    {
        $rows = collect(RoleMatrixData::matrix($role->id))
            ->filter(static fn (RoleMatrixEntry $row): bool => isset(self::SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT[$row->scope->value]))
            ->unique(fn (RoleMatrixEntry $row): string => "{$row->entityKey}|{$row->scope->value}");

        $warnings = [];

        foreach ($rows as $row) {
            $warning = $this->capabilityDriftWarning($role, $row->entityKey, $row->scope->value);

            if ($warning !== null) {
                $warnings[] = $warning;
            }
        }

        return $warnings;
    }

    private function capabilityDriftWarning(RoleView $role, string $entityKey, string $scope): ?string
    {
        if (! $this->entities->has($entityKey)) {
            return null;
        }

        $entity = $this->entities->get($entityKey);
        $requirement = self::SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT[$scope];

        if (in_array($requirement['capability'], $entity->capabilities, true)) {
            return null;
        }

        if (! $this->schema()->hasColumn($entity->table, $requirement['column'])) {
            return null;
        }

        return sprintf(
            "Role '%s' matrix has entity '%s' with scope '%s', which requires capability '%s' — the entity's table has column '%s' but its EntityDefinition does not declare that capability.",
            $role->slug,
            $entityKey,
            $scope,
            $requirement['capability']->value,
            $requirement['column'],
        );
    }

    private function schema(): SchemaBuilder
    {
        /** @var Connection */
        $connection = $this->connections->connection();

        return $connection->getSchemaBuilder();
    }
}

A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Tests\TestCase;

require_once __DIR__.'/TestCase.php';
require_once __DIR__.'/Stubs/ContextUser.php';
require_once __DIR__.'/Stubs/Project.php';

uses(TestCase::class)->in('Feature');

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\AccessAzguard\Tests;

use AzGuard\AzGuardServiceProvider;
use CoreX\Access\CoreAuthServiceProvider;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\AccessAzguardServiceProvider;
use CoreX\CoreServiceProvider;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\EntityRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\Contracts\ModuleRegistry;
use CoreX\Modules\ModulesServiceProvider;
use CoreX\Modules\Testing\ArrayEntityRegistry;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Application;
use Orchestra\Testbench\TestCase as Orchestra;

abstract class TestCase extends Orchestra
{
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        parent::setUp();

        $this->artisan('migrate', ['--force' => true])->run();
    }

    /** @param Application $app */
    protected function getPackageProviders($app): array
    {
        return [CoreServiceProvider::class, ModulesServiceProvider::class, AzGuardServiceProvider::class,
            CoreAuthServiceProvider::class, AccessAzguardServiceProvider::class];
    }

    /** @param Application $app */
    protected function defineEnvironment($app): void
    {
        $app->singleton(ArrayEntityRegistry::class, static fn (Application $app): ArrayEntityRegistry => new ArrayEntityRegistry(
            moduleActive: static fn (string $module, mixed $ctx): bool => $app->make(ModuleRegistry::class)->isActive($module, $ctx),
        ));
        $app->singleton(EntityRegistry::class, static fn (Application $app): ArrayEntityRegistry => $app->make(ArrayEntityRegistry::class));

        $app['config']->set('database.default', 'testbench');
        $app['config']->set('database.connections.testbench', [
            'driver' => 'sqlite', 'database' => ':memory:', 'prefix' => '',
        ]);
    }

    protected function defineDatabaseMigrations(): void
    {
        $this->loadMigrationsFrom(__DIR__.'/database/migrations');
    }
}

# Changelog

## Unreleased — P07.4

- Introduced the optional AzGuard bridge for native CoreX Access authorization.
- Moved the AzGuard context guard, permission layer, grant source, catalog builder, and role model adapter out of `corex-access`.
- Added synchronous matrix mirroring and the tenant-local `aut_azguard_role_links` table.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Enums;

use CoreX\Attributes\Api;

#[Api(since: '1.0')]
enum PrincipalType: string
{
    case User = 'user';
    case Agent = 'agent';
    case ApiKey = 'api_key';
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use AzGuard\Contracts\ContextGuard;
use AzGuard\Contracts\PermissionLayer;
use AzGuard\Models\Role;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\AccessAzguardRegistrar;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\AccessAzguardServiceProvider;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\AccessAzguardOptions;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\AzGuardRoleModel;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\TenantContextGuard;
use CoreX\AccessAzguard\Internal\WorkspacePermissionLayer;
use CoreX\Config\Exceptions\InvalidConfiguration;
use Illuminate\Config\Repository;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Application;

it('resolves bridge options as a shared immutable snapshot', function (): void {
    $options = app(AccessAzguardOptions::class);
    config()->set('corex-access-azguard.azguard_pins.table_names.roles', 'changed_roles');

    expect(app(AccessAzguardOptions::class))->toBe($options)
        ->and($options->rolesTable)->toBe('az_guard_roles');
    expect(function () use ($options): void {
        $options->rolesTable = 'mutable_roles';
    })->toThrow(Error::class);
});

it('keeps the shared bridge options unresolved during registration', function (): void {
    $application = new Application;
    $application->instance('config', new Repository);
    (new AccessAzguardServiceProvider($application))->register();

    expect($application->resolved(AccessAzguardOptions::class))->toBeFalse();
    $application->make('config')->set('corex-access-azguard.bind_permission_layer', false);
    $options = $application->make(AccessAzguardOptions::class);
    expect($options->bindPermissionLayer)->toBeFalse()
        ->and($application->make(AccessAzguardOptions::class))->toBe($options);
});

it('applies bridge pins through the public registrar over conflicting AzGuard config', function (): void {
    config()->set('az-guard.table_names.roles', 'external_roles');
    config()->set('az-guard.column_names.morph_type', 'int');
    config()->set('az-guard.models.role', Role::class);
    config()->set('corex-access-azguard.azguard_pins.table_names.roles', 'bridge_roles');

    (new AccessAzguardRegistrar)->register($this->app);

    expect(config('az-guard.table_names.roles'))->toBe('bridge_roles')
        ->and(config('az-guard.column_names.morph_type'))->toBe('uuid')
        ->and(config('az-guard.models.role'))->toBe(AzGuardRoleModel::class)
        ->and(app(ContextGuard::class))->toBeInstanceOf(TenantContextGuard::class)
        ->and(app(PermissionLayer::class))->toBeInstanceOf(WorkspacePermissionLayer::class);
});

it('retains an existing permission layer binding when bridge binding is disabled', function (): void {
    config()->set('corex-access-azguard.bind_permission_layer', false);
    $layer = Mockery::mock(PermissionLayer::class);
    app()->instance(PermissionLayer::class, $layer);

    (new AccessAzguardRegistrar)->register($this->app);

    expect(app(PermissionLayer::class))->toBe($layer);
});

it('has usable bridge options defaults on an empty configuration', function (): void {
    $options = AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray([]);

    expect($options->bindPermissionLayer)->toBeTrue()
        ->and($options->rolesTable)->toBe('az_guard_roles')
        ->and($options->morphType)->toBe('uuid')
        ->and($options->roleModel)->toBe(AzGuardRoleModel::class);
});

it('accepts the documented AzGuard pin override shapes', function (): void {
    $options = AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray([
        'bind_permission_layer' => false,
        'azguard_pins' => [
            'table_names' => ['roles' => 'custom_roles'],
            'column_names' => ['morph_type' => 'ulid'],
            'models' => ['role' => Role::class],
        ],
    ]);

    expect($options->bindPermissionLayer)->toBeFalse()
        ->and($options->rolesTable)->toBe('custom_roles')
        ->and($options->morphType)->toBe('ulid')
        ->and($options->roleModel)->toBe(Role::class)
        ->and(AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray(['azguard_pins' => ['models' => ['role' => null]]])->roleModel)->toBeNull();
});

it('rejects invalid bridge configuration with the offending path', function (array $config, string $path): void {
    try {
        AccessAzguardOptions::fromArray($config);
        $this->fail('Invalid bridge configuration was accepted.');
    } catch (InvalidConfiguration $exception) {
        expect($exception->violations)->toHaveCount(1)
            ->and($exception->violations[0])->toStartWith($path.':');
    }
})->with([
    'binding flag' => [['bind_permission_layer' => 'true'], 'bind_permission_layer'],
    'pin group' => [['azguard_pins' => 'invalid'], 'azguard_pins'],
    'tables group' => [['azguard_pins' => ['table_names' => false]], 'azguard_pins.table_names'],
    'roles table' => [['azguard_pins' => ['table_names' => ['roles' => '']]], 'azguard_pins.table_names.roles'],
    'morph type' => [['azguard_pins' => ['column_names' => ['morph_type' => 'bad']]], 'azguard_pins.column_names.morph_type'],
    'role model' => [['azguard_pins' => ['models' => ['role' => stdClass::class]]], 'azguard_pins.models.role'],
]);

it('validates the lazy bridge options before booting runtime integrations', function (): void {
    $application = new Application;
    $application->instance('config', new Repository);
    $provider = new AccessAzguardServiceProvider($application);
    $provider->register();
    $application->make('config')->set('corex-access-azguard.bind_permission_layer', 'invalid');

    expect(fn () => $provider->boot())->toThrow(InvalidConfiguration::class);
});

1→# Changelog

## Unreleased — native authorization (P07.4)

- Breaking before 1.0: access evaluates its own role matrix and direct grants; AzGuard integration moved to the optional `corex-access-azguard` package.
- Added `aut_direct_grants` and the `RoleMatrixCompiled` event. Compilation dispatches synchronously in the tenant transaction and invalidates scope versions after commit.
- Removed `aut_roles.azguard_role_id`, `RoleView::azguardRoleId`, `RoleMatrixData::bindAzGuardRole`, and AzGuard options. Access checks deny inactive entities before reading cached scopes or grants.

## Unreleased — thin providers and registrars (P05.2)
10→
- `CoreAuthServiceProvider` delegates to `AccessBindingsRegistrar` and `AccessIntegrationRegistrar`; bindings, order and lifetimes are unchanged.

## Unreleased — typed Options and runtime configuration checks (P05.1)

- `AuthOptions` is a lazy shared singleton resolved in `boot()`; it is no longer bound with `instance()` while the provider registers.

## Unreleased — kernel package and API migration

- Breaking (PLAN3.P02–P04, pre-1.0): Authorization now exposes Principal, RecordContext and AccessChecker ports plus typed AuthOptions and matrix registration; AzGuard identities and permission storage remain implementation details.
20→- Package installation uses the `axiomasoft` Composer vendor and PHP 8.4–8.5 / Laravel 12–13 constraints; `resources/contracts/php-api.json` records the explicitly attributed API and SPI. Old names have no compatibility aliases.

## Unreleased — PHP surface strict cutover

- Breaking (PLAN3.P04, pre-1.0): supported PHP symbols are declared individually with Api/Spi attributes. Concrete implementation types moved to Internal and typed ports/DTOs and error contracts replace predecessor surfaces as recorded in PLAN3.D63/D64; namespace metadata no longer grants compatibility.
- Generated `resources/contracts/php-api.json` records supported layers and signatures. Strict source/graph/BC checks enforce the declared surface; Internal has no external BC promise.

## Unreleased — typed error contract (P04.3)

- Added package owned error enums, definitions and safe coded exception descriptors.
30→- Error constructors require enum identities; existing error wire values are scoped.
- Contributions are validated and frozen at boot; persisted identities use validated lookup.

## Unreleased — package identifier alignment

### Changed

- PLAN3.D57: implementation classes moved to `<Module>\Internal\…`, public types to module categories
  (`Contracts|Data|Enums|Events|Exceptions`); see `docs/architecture/constitution.md` STR-003. Drain queues before
  upgrading; stored `*_type` values holding an old model FQCN no longer resolve (no aliases, PLAN3.D01).
40→
- Breaking before 1.0: Rename config and publish identifiers to `corex-access` and environment variables to `COREX_ACCESS_*`.

Все заметные изменения `corex/auth` документируются здесь. Формат — [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).
Пакет pre-1.0 — breaking-изменения публичных контрактов легальны в MINOR до 1.0 (D17).

## [Unreleased]

- PHP API manifests now record direct inheritance, interfaces and traits separately and include only members declared by this package; external dependency members are omitted without changing the `php-api/1` schema.

50→### Changed

- Password rehash delegates to the identity table owner's `IdentityPasswordRehasher` port with compare-and-swap inputs; auth no longer updates `users` directly.
- P7.7: `DefaultAccessChecker`, matrix/access helpers и компилятор матрицы
  получают `AuthOptions` вместо прямых вызовов `config('corex-auth.*')`.
- P7.6: `AuthOptions::fromArray` валидирует снимок `corex-auth`; провайдер и
  `PrincipalUserProvider` читают identity и pins из Options.
- Released metadata no longer declares development `path` repositories or an
  unconfirmed AzGuard remote. Private AzGuard resolution is a consumer-owned,
  canonical immutable channel; credentials are never stored in this package.
60→
## [0.1.0] - 2026-07-27

First tagged release — roadmap-фаза P1 / B-11 (AzGuard-мост, entity-scoped RBAC, OIDC).
Repo-level tag `v0.2.0` per D17 default policy (no per-package split mirror configured).

### Added

- **Local login lane / principal seam (P2.22, D125).** `Identity\PrincipalUserProvider
  implements Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\UserProvider` — all six interface methods, table/columns
70→  entirely from `config('corex-auth.identity')` (`connection`/`table`/column map), queries via
  `DB::connection($conn)->table($table)` (no `corex/tenancy` model import, AC-28). The "live
  user" filter (`active = true AND deleted_at IS NULL`) is applied in BOTH `retrieveById()` and
  `retrieveByCredentials()` — a deactivated user's live session does not outlive the
  deactivation. `retrieveByCredentials()` ignores the `password` key when building the WHERE
  (Laravel canon) and matches e-mail case-insensitively (`whereRaw('lower(...) = ?')` — the
  schema's unique index is exactly that). `validateCredentials()` is `Hash::check()` only, never
  a string comparison. `rehashPasswordIfRequired()` issues an `UPDATE` iff
  `Hash::needsRehash($hash) || $force`, otherwise zero queries. `retrieveByToken()`/
  `updateRememberToken()` are permanent no-ops — `users` (P2.7, frozen DDL) carries no
80→  `remember_token` column and one will not be added.

1→# axiomasoft/corex-access

Native authorization for CoreX. The package owns tenant role matrices, role assignments, direct grants and scope checks. It works without an external authorization engine.

## Authorization

`AccessChecker::allowed()` checks an active role assignment in the current workspace with a non-`none` matrix row, then an active `aut_direct_grants` row. Unknown or inactive entities always deny. Direct grants must match the principal type, UUID and `{panel}.{entity_key}.{action}` permission key; expired or revoked grants deny.

`scopeFor()` computes the effective role scope. `canOnRecord()` and `ScopeResolver::apply()` share the scope predicate and deny inactive entities before consulting direct grants. An active direct grant bypasses the record scope predicate. Scope normalization rejects a missing capability when the backing table has its corresponding column.
10→
`RoleMatrixCompiler::compile()` publishes `RoleMatrixCompiled` synchronously on the tenant connection. A listener failure rolls back the transaction; the scope map version changes only after commit. The optional bridge listens to this event.

The package publishes tenant migrations for `aut_roles`, `aut_role_assignments`, `aut_role_matrix` and `aut_direct_grants`. The consuming application assembles these in its tenant schema. It may additionally publish the separate cloud FK migrations when the dependent tables exist.

## Extension contracts

Consumers bind `CoreX\Access\Matrix\Contracts\EntityActivity` to decide whether an entity is active and may implement `CoreX\Access\Contracts\RoleMatrixCompiler` when using another compiler. The default bindings are installed by `CoreAuthServiceProvider`.

## Identity provider
20→
`PrincipalUserProvider` registers the `corex-principal` Laravel auth driver. Configure `corex-access.identity` for the user table and columns, then opt into the driver in the application's own auth configuration:

```php
'providers' => [
    'users' => ['driver' => 'corex-principal'],
],
```

The provider reads users through the configured connection and returns `PrincipalIdentity`. It does not write `auth.*` configuration. Password rehashing uses `IdentityPasswordRehasher`; remember tokens are unsupported.
30→
## Installation

Install `axiomasoft/corex-access`, configure the package and assemble its migrations on the intended tenant connection. Composer repositories are application owned and are not inherited from dependencies.

## Development

```bash
composer install
composer test
40→composer test:pg
composer analyse
composer lint:check
```

1→# axiomasoft/corex-access

Native authorization for CoreX. The package owns tenant role matrices, role assignments, direct grants and scope checks. It works without an external authorization engine.

## Authorization

`AccessChecker::allowed()` checks an active role assignment in the current workspace with a non-`none` matrix row, then an active `aut_direct_grants` row. Unknown or inactive entities always deny. Direct grants must match the principal type, UUID and `{panel}.{entity_key}.{action}` permission key; expired or revoked grants deny.

`scopeFor()` computes the effective role scope. `canOnRecord()` and `ScopeResolver::apply()` share the scope predicate and deny inactive entities before consulting direct grants. An active direct grant bypasses the record scope predicate. Scope normalization rejects a missing capability when the backing table has its corresponding column.
10→
`RoleMatrixCompiler::compile()` publishes `RoleMatrixCompiled` synchronously on the tenant connection. A listener failure rolls back the transaction; the scope map version changes only after commit. The optional bridge listens to this event.

The package publishes tenant migrations for `aut_roles`, `aut_role_assignments`, `aut_role_matrix` and `aut_direct_grants`. The consuming application assembles these in its tenant schema. It may additionally publish the separate cloud FK migrations when the dependent tables exist.

## Extension contracts

Consumers bind `CoreX\Access\Matrix\Contracts\EntityActivity` to decide whether an entity is active and may implement `CoreX\Access\Contracts\RoleMatrixCompiler` when using another compiler. The default bindings are installed by `CoreAuthServiceProvider`.

## Identity provider
20→
`PrincipalUserProvider` registers the `corex-principal` Laravel auth driver. Configure `corex-access.identity` for the user table and columns, then opt into the driver in the application's own auth configuration:

```php
'providers' => [
    'users' => ['driver' => 'corex-principal'],
],
```

The provider reads users through the configured connection and returns `PrincipalIdentity`. It does not write `auth.*` configuration. Password rehashing uses `IdentityPasswordRehasher`; remember tokens are unsupported.
30→
## Installation

Install `axiomasoft/corex-access`, configure the package and assemble its migrations on the intended tenant connection. Composer repositories are application owned and are not inherited from dependencies.

## Development

```bash
composer install
composer test
40→composer test:pg
composer analyse
composer lint:check
```

1→# axiomasoft/corex-access-azguard

Optional AzGuard integration for `axiomasoft/corex-access`. The native Access role matrix remains authoritative. When Access compiles a role, this bridge mirrors its active permission keys into AzGuard and stores the role ID link in `aut_azguard_role_links`.

The bridge also registers AzGuard's context guard, workspace cache discriminator, matrix grant source, permission catalog builder, role model pin, and `@scope` / `@entity` Blade directives. Access works without this package.

## Installation

The package is unreleased while AzGuard has no stable published release. Configure the application-owned Composer channel for `axioma-studio/azguard-core` and install this bridge only in a consumer that opts into AzGuard. Composer repositories in a dependency are not inherited by that consumer.
10→
Publish and apply `corex-access` tenant migrations, then publish and apply `corex-access-azguard-migrations-tenant`. The bridge migration creates `aut_azguard_role_links`; it does not change `aut_roles`. Publish `corex-access-azguard-config` to change the AzGuard pins or disable this package's singular `PermissionLayer` binding when another integration owns it.

The listener runs synchronously inside Access compilation's tenant transaction. An exception rolls back native compilation and the mirror. A missing role is an error. Without this bridge, Access compiles and evaluates permissions through its own data.

 * pattern as the module-activation-gate boxed/cloud seam.
 *
 * @internal spec: D10, B-11 §6.1 L892–907
 */
final class NullTenancyManager implements TenancyManager
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly TenantContextResolver $resolver,
    ) {}

    public function context(): TenantContext
    {
        return $this->resolver->current();
    }

    public function initialized(): bool
    {
        return true;
    }

    public function initialize(AccountRef $account): void
    {
        // no-op — boxed installs run a single constant account.
    }

    public function setWorkspace(?WorkspaceRef $workspace): void
    {
        // no-op — boxed installs have no workspace tier.
    }

    public function end(): void
    {
        // no-op.
    }

    public function runFor(AccountRef $account, ?WorkspaceRef $workspace, Closure $callback): mixed
    {
        return $callback();
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Context\Contracts;

use Closure;
use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Context\Data\AccountRef;
use CoreX\Context\Data\TenantContext;
use CoreX\Context\Data\WorkspaceRef;

/**
 * Single point of tenant-context switching (connection/cache/session/queue).
 * Boxed installs bind a null-manager (constant context); cloud installs bind
 * the implementation of `axiomasoft/corex-tenancy` — the choice is a container
 * binding, never an `if(cloud)` branch.
 *
 * Switching semantics of the cloud implementation (PLAN3.D95):
 * - `initialize()` of another account ends the current one first; the same account is a no-op;
 * - every switch — `initialize()`, `end()`, leaving `runFor()` — forgets the container's scoped
 *   instances, so a scoped service resolved inside a context holds that context's connection and
 *   one resolved before a switch must not be kept across it;
 * - `runFor()` restores the previous account and workspace in `finally`, also after a failure;
 * - a failed restoration poisons the runtime: it refuses every further call until the
 *   application is recreated.
 */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Implement, since: '1.0')]
interface TenancyManager
{
    /**
     * The active context, or null when running in the central/root scope
     * (not inside any tenant).
     */
    public function context(): ?TenantContext;

    public function initialized(): bool;

    public function initialize(AccountRef $account): void;

    /**
     * Narrows (or clears, with null) the workspace within the already-
     * initialized account context. No-op on the boxed null-manager.
     */
    public function setWorkspace(?WorkspaceRef $workspace): void;

    public function end(): void;

    /**
     * Runs `$callback` inside the given account/workspace context, then
     * unconditionally reverts (finally) — the seam for control-plane sweeps
     * and cron jobs run outside a request cycle.
     *
     * @template T
     *
     * @param  Closure(): T  $callback
     * @return T
     */
    public function runFor(AccountRef $account, ?WorkspaceRef $workspace, Closure $callback): mixed;
}

namespace CoreX\Context\Internal;

use CoreX\Context\Contracts\TenantContextResolver;
use CoreX\Context\Data\AccountRef;
use CoreX\Context\Data\TenantContext;

/**
 * Boxed-install stub: a deterministic constant TenantContext, no config
 * lookup, no workspace. Real resolvers (host/root, axiomasoft/corex-tenancy) land
 * later.
 *
 * @internal spec: D10
 */
final class SingleAccountResolver implements TenantContextResolver
{
    private const ACCOUNT_ID = '00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000000';

    private const ACCOUNT_SLUG = 'boxed';

    private const ACCOUNT_STATUS = 'active';

    public function current(): TenantContext
    {
        return new TenantContext(
            account: new AccountRef(
                id: self::ACCOUNT_ID,
                slug: self::ACCOUNT_SLUG,
                status: self::ACCOUNT_STATUS,
                features: [],
                limits: [],
            ),
            workspace: null,
            boxed: true,
        );
    }
}

use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Override;

/**
 * @property int $id
 * @property string $name
 * @property int $level
 * @property string|null $class_name
 * @property Carbon|null $created_at
 * @property Carbon|null $updated_at
 */
class Role extends Model
{
    /**
     * class_name is deliberately NOT fillable (C-11): it wires the role to a
     * PHP RoleInterface class (getRoleLogic()) and must only be set through
     * trusted internal paths (e.g. RoleAssignmentCommand's direct setter),
     * never from mass-assigned request input.
     */
    protected $fillable = ['name', 'level'];

    #[Override]
    public function getTable(): string
    {
        return Config::rolesTable();
    }

    /** @return MorphToMany<Model, $this> */
    public function users(): MorphToMany
    {
        /** @var class-string<Model> $userModel */
        $userModel = config('auth.providers.users.model');

        return $this->morphedByMany(
            $userModel,
            'model',
            Config::modelHasRolesTable(),
            'role_id',
            'model_id',
        );
    }

    /**
     * Permissions assigned to the role via the DB (not via PHP class).
     * Used by DatabaseRoleGrantSource.
     *
     * @return HasMany<RolePermission, $this>
     */
    public function dbPermissions(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(

    }

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

**Actor:** author-choice (claude-opus-5-5/high) по мандату владельца «есть идеальное решение — утверждай» (`brief/00-brief.md` B6)
**Evidence:** RAG:— `findings/00-audit-verification.md`, `artifacts/P00-design/facts/`; RAG:✅ `research/01-external-research.md`, `artifacts/research-rag/`

## Solution

`corex-access` владеет контрактами авторизации платформы (tenant-boundary, entity-context, scope) без зависимости от AzGuard; интеграция с AzGuard — отдельный integration-пакет-мост, требующий опубликованный стабильный релиз AzGuard. Namespace `CoreX\Auth` → по glossary (`CoreX\Access`). Никаких VCS/`@dev` зависимостей в релизных пакетах.

## Why
20→
F00 A2.4, A14.1; доктрина: «AzGuard независимо владеет своей ролевой системой … access может документировать необязательный адаптер» (`docs/dev-doctrine.md` §1).

## Consequences

P07; owner-gate публикации AzGuard (вне репо) — только для моста.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace AzGuard\Concerns;

use AzGuard\Contracts\AzGuardManagerInterface;
use AzGuard\Contracts\ContextGuard;
use AzGuard\Contracts\PermissionContext;
use AzGuard\Contracts\PermissionResolverInterface;
use AzGuard\Panels\PanelResolver;
use AzGuard\Permissions\PermissionName;
use AzGuard\Registry\Values\PermissionSet;
use AzGuard\Runtime\RequestState;
use BackedEnum;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
use Throwable;
use UnitEnum;

trait HasPermissions
{
    /**
     * Check if the user has a permission on a panel.
     *
     * $permission may be a fully-qualified key string ("app.posts.edit") or a
     * permission enum case, which is scoped to the panel automatically.
     *
     * Optional $context allows a one-off contextual check without changing
     * global state. Use hasPermissionIn() as a more readable alternative.
     */
    public function hasPermission(string|UnitEnum $permission, string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null, ?PermissionContext $context = null): bool
    {
        $panelId = PanelResolver::resolveDefault($panelId === null ? null : PanelResolver::normalizeId($panelId));
        $key = PermissionName::resolve($permission, $panelId);

        if ($context instanceof PermissionContext) {
            $guard = $this->contextGuard();

            // No context package installed — fall back to a global check.
            return $guard === null
                ? $this->permissionSet($panelId)->grants($key)
                : $guard->checkInContext($this, $context->contextType(), $context->contextId(), $key, $panelId);
        }

        return $this->permissionSet($panelId)->grants($key);
    }

    /**
     * Contextual permission check — does not mutate global state.
     *
     *   $user->hasPermissionIn('workspace', 42, 'app.posts.edit');
     *   $user->hasPermissionIn('workspace', 42, 'app.posts.edit', 'admin');
     */
    public function hasPermissionIn(
        string $contextType,
        int|string $contextId,
        string|UnitEnum $permission,
        string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null,
    ): bool {
        $panelId = PanelResolver::resolveDefault($panelId === null ? null : PanelResolver::normalizeId($panelId));
        $guard = $this->contextGuard();

        if ($guard === null) {
            // Silent false is intentional (global fallback), but observable: warn
            // once per request so a missing context backend is not a silent
            // false-negative. RequestState is a scoped binding (flushed per
            // request) — Octane-safe, unlike a static flag which would warn once
            // per worker only.
            app(RequestState::class)->once(
                'context-guard-missing',
                static function (): void {
                    Log::warning(
                        'AzGuard: hasPermissionIn() called but no ContextGuard is bound; returning false. '
                        .'Install azguard/context or bind '.ContextGuard::class.' to enable contextual checks.',
                    );
                },
            );

            return false;

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace AzGuard\Contracts;

use AzGuard\Registry\Values\PermissionSet;
use BackedEnum;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
use UnitEnum;

/**
 * Public contract for the permission-checking surface of an AzGuard user.
 *
 * Mirrors the {@see \AzGuard\Concerns\HasPermissions} trait 1:1 — declare this
 * interface on your User model and `use` the trait to satisfy it with no extra
 * code. Type-hint this (or the composite {@see AzGuardUser}) instead of a trait,
 * which cannot be type-hinted.
 *
 * @api
 */
interface HasPermissions
{
    public function hasPermission(string|UnitEnum $permission, string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null, ?PermissionContext $context = null): bool;

    public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string|UnitEnum $permission, string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null): bool;

    public function checkPermission(string|UnitEnum $permission, string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null, ?PermissionContext $context = null): bool;

    public function permissionSet(string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null): PermissionSet;

    /** @return Collection<int, string> */
    public function permissions(string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null): Collection;

    public function isSuperAdmin(string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null): bool;

    public function flushPermissions(string|BackedEnum|null $panelId = null): void;

    public function hasContextGuard(): bool;
}

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: bundled:review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.
